title: Introduce build-hints shim and consolidate language toolchain images to shrink CI runtime
creator: Ava Patel
description: Problem: Our CI pipelines have accumulated multiple, largely overlapping language/toolchain images (node/python/go/rust) and per-repo ad-hoc install steps. This increases CI cold-start time, inflates ephemeral image sizes, and reduces cache hit rates across projects. We've also seen flaky lint steps because different repos pin slightly different versions of linters and formatters. Goal: reduce CI median job runtime by ~20-30% for core repos and simplify local dev parity by introducing a lightweight 'build-hints' shim that exposes per-repo metadata for smarter cache priming, and consolidating language runtimes into a small set of curated base images (minimal, dev, and test) with deterministic toolchains baked in. Deliverables: 1) build-hints shim library (bash/python) that emits a small JSON manifest per repo with required toolchains, common build targets, and cache hints; 2) three curated base images (redwood/base-minimal, redwood/base-dev, redwood/base-test) with locked toolchain versions and layer ordering optimized for cache reuse; 3) CI config changes (BuildKit + remote cache via our s3-backed CAS) to prime caches based on build-hints and to decouple linting into a fast, cached job; 4) migration guide and developer shim for local docker/buildx devflow. Acceptance criteria: - Core platform repo median CI runtime reduced by >=20% on blue-green runs - Cache hit rate for layer keys increased by 35% compared to baseline - Linter flakiness incidents reduced to zero for three cycles - Migration docs + one-week rollout plan published and approved in docs PR
steps: Design build-hints schema and CLI shim (prototype in python) — include toolchain names/versions, expected heavy directories, primary build targets
Build and publish three curated base images (minimal/dev/test) with reproducible layer ordering
Enable BuildKit remote cache and hook cache priming step that consumes build-hints manifest
Introduce separate lint job that uses pre-baked linter layers and fast exit on no-changes
Run pilot on repo: redwood-serving-runtime and measure baseline vs after-change
Rollout to top-10 repos by CI runtime, monitor, and iterate on image size and toolchain pins
progress_updates: 2026-02-18: Ticket created after infra retro — identified CI runtime as recurring pain across teams (Ava)

2026-02-28: PoC base image redwood/base-minimal built and pushed to ECR; size reduced by ~42% vs legacy node-python image for a minimal JS repo (local bench)
2026-03-03: Experimented with BuildKit remote cache; initial cache key policy caused churn — changed key to include ordered toolchain tuple and heavy_paths digest (worked better)
2026-03-06: Pilot integrated into redwood-serving-runtime CI: median job time reduced from 12m -> 8m on cold runs (33% improvement) and warm-run cache hit improved ~38% (benchmarks in dashboard)

2026-03-10: Found trade-off: baking all linters into base images increases image churn when one linter updates. Decided to keep linters in separate linter-layer image with semver pinning and per-repo override allowed
2026-03-12: Draft migration guide published: docs/confluence/ci-modernization/build-hints-rollout (link below). Preparing PR to change 5 more repos in the next cycle (Riley to review)
